classification.difficultyReason: Count unordered pairs and identify edge-sharing pairs in a geometric arrangement.

content.prompt: There are nine squares in the figure below, and two of these are chosen at random. Find the probability that the squares share an edge.

spec.description: Nine equal unlabelled squares form a cross. Decorative turquoise source fill is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: A vertical column of five cells and a horizontal row of five cells share their central cell; all individual cell boundaries are visible. There are eight unordered edge-sharing pairs.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied cross is visible; no counting annotations or answers.

answer.short:
$\frac{2}{9}$.

There are 8 edge-sharing pairs among 36 possible pairs.
answer.worked:
There are 4 edge-sharing pairs along the horizontal row and 4 along the vertical column, giving 8 favourable pairs. Each unordered pair of distinct squares is equally likely.

$$\begin{align*}
N_{\text{pairs}}&=\frac{9\times8}{2}\\
N_{\text{pairs}}&=36\\
\Pr(\text{share an edge})&=\frac{8}{36}\\
\Pr(\text{share an edge})&=\frac{2}{9}
\end{align*}$$
